recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片可見多顆較小、深染且無中央淡染區的球形紅血球（spherocytes），夾雜體積較大、偏藍的多染性紅血球（A）；超活體染色顯示大量含網狀沉澱物的網狀紅血球（B），呈現溶血伴骨髓代償反應。
features: Numerous spherocytes: small, dense, round red cells lacking central pallor
Anisocytosis with larger polychromatophilic (bluish-gray) red cells
Occasional red cells with retained central pallor; no significant schistocytes or agglutinates in this field
Supravital stain shows markedly increased reticulocytes with blue-staining reticular RNA precipitates
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous spherocytes with loss of central pallor, anisocytosis and polychromasia; schistocytes and red cell agglutination are not evident in this field. White cell morphology in the visible neutrophil is unremarkable. A supravital (new methylene blue) preparation shows a markedly increased proportion of reticulocytes containing precipitated reticular material. The findings indicate spherocytic hemolysis with a brisk marrow response; together with a positive direct antiglobulin test, they are consistent with autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

ddx.vs: HS shows identical spherocytes but has a negative DAT, family history and abnormal EMA-binding flow cytometry, so morphology alone cannot separate it from warm AIHA.
MAHA shows schistocytes (helmet cells, triangles) with thrombocytopenia rather than predominantly round spherocytes.
Clostridial toxin and thermal injury produce microspherocytes with fragments and budding (and in sepsis, ghost cells) in the appropriate clinical setting.
CAD shows red cell agglutinates in clumps on the smear and a C3d-only DAT, with fewer spherocytes than warm IgG AIHA.
